data.narrative:
Lumaril is a Seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Mark Elliot and Ben Duffield that has raised $12M to date. The sector peer set comprises nine private companies and one public comparable (277810.KQ), including names such as Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, and Locus Robotics, though no tight clustering of same-stage or similar-tier peers exists sufficient for median-based triangulation.

A Stage-Progression methodology is applicable and yields a $30M implied valuation. This approach applies a typical Seed-to-next-stage step-up multiplier of 2.5x to the $12M total raised proxy, reflecting the expected value creation milestone between funding rounds in this sector. The Peer-Median method is not applicable: while 11 same-sector robotics peers exist in the broader dataset, filtering for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier comps returns fewer than three datapoints, rendering a median comparison uninformative relative to an all-sector average.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $26M (low) to $34M (high), with a central estimate of $30M. This range reflects the single methodological input and corresponding estimation uncertainty. Key risks to valuation include the nascency of the peer set in frontier robotics, the heavy reliance on stage-progression multipliers rather than market comparables, and the binary nature of Seed-stage outcome distributions. Additional data on comparable financials or follow-on round terms would strengthen conviction in this range.
